blocks.text: Why Excel is essential for book publicists

Your day as a publicist involves constant coordination. You manage media lists, track interview requests, and report on book coverage. Excel acts as the backbone for this data. When you keep your media contacts in a structured spreadsheet, you can filter by outlet, beat, or location instantly. This beats searching through scattered email threads.
Getting started with Excel on Mac

First, ensure your Excel version is up to date. Microsoft 365 for Mac runs best on the latest macOS versions. If you find the interface cluttered, you can hide gridlines to focus on your data. Go to the View tab and uncheck Gridlines. This makes your media list look like a clean document.

items: Create distinct columns for Name, Outlet, Email, and Last Contacted Date.
Use Data Validation to create drop down lists for contact status.
Freeze the top row so your headers stay visible as you scroll.
Use conditional formatting to highlight contacts you have not pitched in over three months.

blocks.text: Speed matters when you have a mountain of press releases to send. Use ⌘ + Space to quickly select a column. Use ⌘ + D to fill data down from the cell above. If you need to edit a cell, press Fn + F2. These small actions add up over a busy day.

When you secure a review or an interview, log it immediately. Create a separate tab for coverage. Include the publication date, the outlet name, and a link to the piece. If you want to see how many placements you secured by month, use a pivot table. Pivot tables summarize large sets of data into clear reports for your authors.

Publicists often face issues with data formatting. Excel might turn your ISBN numbers into scientific notation. To fix this, set the column format to Text before you paste your data. Another common mistake is having duplicate entries in your media list. Use the Data tab and select Remove Duplicates to keep your list clean.
If you are unsure how to use a specific function like VLOOKUP or XLOOKUP, hold ⌥ ⌘ and ask Lazur to explain it. Lazur can walk you through the steps while you look at your sheet.

faq.question: Can I use Excel on my Mac without a subscription?
faq.answer: You can use Excel for the web for free, but the desktop application for Mac requires a Microsoft 365 subscription or a one-time purchase of Office 2024.

faq.question: How do I make my media list easier to read?
faq.answer: Try freezing the top row, applying alternating row colors, and using the filter tool to hide contacts that are not relevant to your current project.

faq.question: Does Lazur work inside Excel?
faq.answer: Lazur is a voice assistant that lives in your Mac notch. It does not click buttons inside Excel, but it can guide you through any task by answering out loud or pointing at menu items.
